name: Skeuomorph
summary: A detail that copies the material or the form of an older object, though it no longer has that function.
how: Copy one material for each surface: leather, felt, wood, paper or brushed metal.
Light every surface from one source above, at 90 degrees.
Keep the old details that tell the use: stitches, page edges, knobs and screws.

origin.note: Doric stone temples carve triglyphs and guttae that copy the beam ends and pegs of earlier timber temples.

adoptions.via: Mac OS X icons draw each application as a real object, such as a stamp, a clock or a disc.
iPhone OS copies notepads, leather, felt and brushed metal in its applications.

sources.title: Donald Norman, The Design of Everyday Things (1988)
